# One isolated publication reconstruction

Read the execution plan and entire allowed reader, including every shared block, in bounded untruncated output. Confirm the sole absolute destination and report complete reading; wait for authenticated controller release before authoring. Only locked source, inventory, resolved judgments and calculated scores are assessment evidence. Reference metrics benchmark exposition only. Do not browse, inspect other debates, peer outputs, sessions, environment or credentials, use paid services or spawn agents. Use the exact model and effort in the plan.

Identity, move selection, sections, positions, source ownership, timecodes, ratings and all scores are frozen. Author only summary, quotes, moves, overall, logicalExtension, noveltyMap and editorialReview. The checker assembles these parts with the frozen skeleton. Never author new score fields or recalculate results.

## Current source and adopted burdens

This assessment covers Sean McDowell and Paulogia’s substantive discussion and final statements, approximately 8:43–1:11:15, with exclusions. Introductions, advertisements, moderator commentary and the host’s argumentative interventions and dependent replies are excluded, including the exchange at approximately 1:00:08–1:08:35. Neither speaker receives credit, penalties, or an inference of failing to reply from excluded material. There were no formal timed rounds or audience Q&A. The scores assess the retained discussion, not the complete recording.

The neutral motion and side labels come only from the frozen skeleton. McDowell offers suffering as support for sincerity and against conscious fabrication, explicitly as one contribution to a larger resurrection case. Paulogia concedes probable Peter/Paul sincerity and deaths, questions the wider group, and distinguishes sincere belief from truth. Neither side must defend a stronger claim than adopted. The late host-led chain is excluded together with every dependent reply, so the earlier independent motivation proposal cannot be presented as unanswered.

All 25 moves and six sections are frozen. Nine below-high-confidence checks are complete. Original caption-only warnings remain historical records; the completed findings below qualify them. No direct audio listening is claimed. The third-criterion clause chose not to die remains literally uncertain and must not be inverted, quoted, treated as an independent premise, or used for a coherence penalty. Player names, garbled classifications and exact recognition-uncertain numbers stay ineligible; clear speaker-level memory qualifications or unsupported reasoning remain assessable. Paulogia immediately retracts nursery rhyme to creed, accepts the early date, and describes a mental-state check as an initial comparison, not categorical rejection. His motive analogy is expressly qualified by not necessarily being willing to die for attention.

## Exact parts schema and limits

- summary: 8–35 words, normally 18–28, accurately describing the locked comparison.
- quotes: {pro:{text,context},con:{text,context}}. Each text is an exact 3–18-word substring of one same-side quoteEligibleExactSpans entry; target 6–14 words. Preserve capitalization and punctuation, and choose clear uncorrupted words. Context is 12–55 words explaining the actual inferential setting. The quotation must express a COMPLETE THOUGHT when read without that context; no unfinished object, premise or conclusion and no omitted meaning-changing condition. Context may clarify a referent but must never complete a fragment. Inspect adjacent source sentences; choose another eligible quote rather than invent completion words. Third-party reported claims must not be presented as the speaker’s own view.
- moves: exactly {moveId,words,critique} for every inventory move in inventory order. Words is 8–55 words; target 22–28 and explain the claim, its offered reason or comparison, and the intended inference without adding premises. Overall mean must be at least the minimum recorded in reference-metrics.json and at most one quarter may be below 20. A source-required short item needs a specific editorial explanation.
- Every critique is 105–130 words and at least 880 characters. Exactly four sentences, in this order, beginning “Strongest feature:”, “Principal limitation:”, “Live burden:”, “Locked score:”. Each ends with terminal punctuation. The last starts “Locked score: N ”, copying N from the corresponding skeleton card. Prefer 120–126 substantive words when needed for the character minimum; do not pad. Avoid sentence-breaking abbreviations.
- overall: {pro:{strengths:[strings],blunders:[{text,links:[]}]},con:{...}}. At least three concrete strengths and two material blunders per side. Each item at least eight words, usually 15–30. Keep links empty for the later blind tag review.
- logicalExtension: {pro:{finalArgument:{thesis,premises,conclusion},newArguments:[{title,text}]},con:{...}}. Thesis at least 12 words; 4–6 premises each at least 12 words; conclusion at least 15 words. Each side has 2–4 genuinely new reinforcing arguments, titles 2–8 words and text 45–130 words. Natural depth near the reference corpus is preferable to barely meeting minima: roughly 25–40 words for thesis/conclusion, 18–30 per premise, 75–110 per reinforcing text, where reasoning warrants it.
- noveltyMap: one record for each side's finalArgument and every newArguments item: {side,field,path,hypothetical:true,sourceMoveIds,explanation}. Paths use dot notation such as candidate.logicalExtension.pro.newArguments.0. Use current move IDs that motivate the refinement. Explain in at least 18 words exactly what the new reasoning adds or repairs relative to those moves; never recycle a novelty sentence.
- editorialReview: {completeSourceCompared:true,allCardStrengthsAndLimitationsReviewed:true,correctBurdenPreserved:true,nonformulaicAiProseReviewed:true,ordinaryPunctuationPreserved:true,noJudgmentOrScoreChanges:true}. Assert each only after actually doing it.

## Editorial obligations before the first save

Compose every description, critique and extension item individually. No sentence banks or swapped-name templates. A strength explains an actual contribution, a limitation identifies an actual unresolved weakness, and the live burden stays with whoever bears it. An objection does not automatically require a complete proof of the contrary worldview. The final sentence explains argumentative performance at the locked score, not procedural compliance. Keep scope/process detail in the source note.

Compare every card directly with its source and resolved judgment. Preserve McDowell’s sincerity and anti-conspiracy contribution as part of a larger case rather than a proof of resurrection; Paulogia’s Peter/Paul concessions and challenge to group extension; the early-creed concession and immediate retraction; ordinary mental-state checking versus categorical rejection; and possible motives versus demonstrated causes. Exact caption errors and disputed recognition details are never speaker weaknesses. Do not infer a missing reply from excluded speech. Use complete grammatical sentences and ordinary punctuation.

The AI Contribution is disclosed once by the site section. Within it, write direct philosophical prose, not provenance announcements such as AI-generated extension, possible extension or repeated a model would framing. Read both sides together: compare openings, first-sentence grammar, paragraph progression and conclusions. Each reinforcing argument must add a distinct inference absent from the source, with an individually specific novelty explanation. Reject interchangeable side-swapped scaffolds, generic setup sentences and invulnerability claims. Preserve logical parallelism where substantive, without forced stylistic variety. Later controller comparison with the independent corpus checks repetition and punctuation.

Tags and blunder links stay empty pending two fresh blind reviews and anonymous adjudication against local definitions. Added ideas and tags never change scores.

## Memory-only review and one submission

Create the parts object in persistent functions.store memory. Run the pinned checker from the execution plan via stdin, with the explicit current debate number; it uses the current run's frozen build packet automatically. Safe single-quoted shell input with correctly escaped apostrophes is acceptable; do not rely on JSON.stringify as shell escaping and do not create a disk draft. The checker may also run --emit to assemble the full candidate in memory/tool output.

Check and correct your candidate before the first hold within this same authorized context, then personally complete the editorial review above. Feed the exact existing UTF-8 parts bytes through stdin to the maintained runner handoff hold using your execution plan. Report its receipt and keep its process alive. The controller reads the entire candidate, reviews it against sources and releases one exact-byte first save. You may not save directly, authorize your own release, overwrite a saved output, or start a new context. A failed hold or saved failure is never silently replaced; preserve diagnostics and wait for bounded controller direction.

value.motion: Are apostolic martyrdom and suffering good evidence for the resurrection?

moves.speaker: Paulogia
moves.claim: Paulogia clearly requires a claimed resurrection eyewitness, a chance to recant, and an actual death-level test rather than mere willingness to suffer or die.
moves.warrant: He explains that the familiar argument about dying for a known lie has force only when the person was positioned to know and the historical case connects that knowledge to the cost imposed.
moves.inference: Broad willingness to suffer or die has less evidential force when eyewitness status, recantation opportunity, or actual death is not established.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: This speaker-owned passage contains Paulogia’s proposed criteria and explanation of why eyewitness status and a death-level test matter, ending before the moderator recap.
moves.attributionRationale: The speaker and the eyewitness, recantation, and actual-death contrast are clear, but one clause in the third criterion is materially uncertain.
moves.audioVerificationReason: Verify the uncertain third-criterion wording, including whether chose not to die was spoken as captioned or was a spoken slip; do not use that clause independently or penalize its coherence.
moves.importanceRationale: This sets con’s test for when martyrdom contacts the motion.

burdenContact.rationale: It specifies the required connection among firsthand knowledge, recantation, and death.

moves.speaker: Sean McDowell
moves.claim: Martyrdom need not require a recorded recantation opportunity when someone publicly persists in a dangerous religious message and is killed in connection with it.
moves.warrant: McDowell appeals to martyrdom scholarship and a modern priest widely called a martyr despite no recorded recantation offer.
moves.inference: Paulogia’s recantation criteria are more restrictive than the category needed to assess apostolic suffering.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: The passage preserves the scholarly definition, illustration, and conclusion against the proposed criteria.
moves.attributionRationale: McDowell directly addresses Paulogia and sustains the same response.
moves.importanceRationale: The definition controls which cases can enter the pro argument.

burdenContact.rationale: It makes costly public proclamation relevant without a recorded recantation scene.

responseComponents.description: Challenges the necessity of an explicit recantation opportunity by offering a broader costly-public-proclamation definition.

moves.speaker: Paulogia
moves.claim: Even granting McDowell’s broader definition would not show that the apostles meet it.
moves.warrant: The sources often do not show what particular apostles preached, why they died, or whether politics rather than resurrection proclamation caused a death.
moves.inference: A permissive definition cannot replace case-specific historical evidence.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: This complete reply begins with the conditional grant and ends with the political-versus-ideological objection.
moves.attributionRationale: The explicit pushback and sustained first-person objections identify Paulogia.
moves.importanceRationale: It separates a definition from the factual burden.

burdenContact.rationale: It insists on evidence connecting each death to the relevant proclamation.

responseComponents.description: Grants the broader definition for argument and disputes that the cited apostolic cases satisfy its factual requirements.

moves.warrant: McDowell expressly places the fate argument as one premise within a larger resurrection case.

moves.inference: The scope of demonstrated eyewitness belief is load-bearing for the motion.
